Words to know.

SoapstoneThe stone of the Hoysala temples. It is soft when quarried and hardens in the air, so carvers could cut very fine detail.
MadanikaA bracket figure of a graceful woman, also called salabhanjika, carved under the eaves of temples such as the Chennakesava temple at Belur, built in 1117.
YaliA mythical guardian with a lion-like body, carved on the pillars and brackets of South Indian temples.
Lost-wax castingThe classic way of making South Indian bronzes: a wax model is coated in clay, the wax is melted out, and molten metal fills the space.

Belur and Halebidu were listed as UNESCO World Heritage Sites in 2023, together with Somanathapura.
